body:
We should be able to test this in a local `yb-ctl` setup, where we:
- bring up RF3 `yb-ctl --rf 3 create`
- remove a master with `./build/latest/bin/yb-admin -master_addresses 127.0.0.1:7100,127.0.0.2:7100,127.0.0.3:7100 change_master_config REMOVE_SERVER 127.0.0.3 7100`
- add that master back with `./build/latest/bin/yb-admin -master_addresses 127.0.0.1:7100,127.0.0.2:7100,127.0.0.3:7100 change_master_config ADD_SERVER 127.0.0.3 7100`

Confirm the master does not get back into the quorum correctly:

```

```

The issue seems to be that the REMOVE SERVER deletes the underlying directories (tablet-meta, data) on that master node and when the ADD SERVER comes in, the directories are not recreated. I will look into how those directories were created in the restart case that Bogdan mentioned above and see how we could make it happen on the add.

It looks like the history of changes to the code for going into shell mode is:

1/ Going into shell mode deleted only certain tablet data and group membership data initially.

2/ With this change - https://github.com/YugaByte/yugabyte-db/commit/c311ad31ef2dc6145c9fd017dbb007769b772129#diff-6ee4802be20bdefa2fec63a189974868R430 -
we overcorrected by deleting all dirs under yb-data, including logs, rocksdb and instance metadata

3/ https://github.com/YugaByte/yugabyte-db/commit/7c845fd8ff1caf636b72eff787892ac2124100c8 then walked back some steps and preserved the google logs directory

I will work on a fix and a possible unit test to capture this issue. We need to retain some of the root level dirs so that the server can bootstrap once again and also preserve instance metadata so that the uuid that is used by the server in memory is preserved across restarts.

issue.title: [docs] [community] Adding/removing nodes to a cluster

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
https://yugabyte-db.slack.com/archives/CG0KQF0GG/p1573085316411700

-- doc Bogdan's comments about REMOVE_SERVER at bottom of thread.

Andrew Liu Nov 6th, 2019 at 4:08 PM
Hi YB team, I was experimenting with adding YB-Master nodes to the cluster. I removed one of the YB-Masters and added it back using yb-admin. In the admin ui, it shows that that node is a NON_PARTICIPANT. What does this mean, and how do I make it a participant again?
12 replies
Also sent to the channel

Karthik Ranganathan  2 months ago
Best folks to answer this question are @Bogdan (YugaByte) @Rahul (YB)

Rahul Desirazu  2 months ago
@Andrew Liu What yb-admin command did you use to remove and add the master?




Andrew Liu  2 months ago
Hi @Rahul (YB), thank you for ur reply! I used yb-admin -master_addresses {addrs} change_master_config ADD_SERVER {ip} {port}, like in the docs. (edited) 
Also sent to the channel

Bogdan Matican:palm_tree:  2 months ago
@Andrew Liu so you used REMOVE_SERVER followed by ADD_SERVER, on the same node? If so, it might be this issue: https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/issues/2007 cc @Sanketh (YB)
bmaticanbmatican
#2007 [docdb] Investigate yb-admin change_master_config REMOVE_SERVER + ADD_SERVER failure
Had a situation today where we had to fix a broken master raft quorum. Removing the broken master worked just fine, but adding it back afterwards failed, with some remote bootstrap messaging about not being able to find tablet-meta files for sys catalog (000....000).
Checking the file system however, there was no data (as expected after REMOVE). We had to restart the master with an empty --master_addresses="" to force it to go in shell mode and then the ADD_SERVER worked just fine.
cc @hectorgcr @rahuldesirazu
Assignees
iSignal
Labels
area/docdb
<https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db|yugabyte/yugabyte-db>yugabyte/yugabyte-db | Aug 8th, 2019 | Added by GitHub

Andrew Liu  2 months ago
@Bogdan (YugaByte) Yup, that's what I did. I experimented with the way you guys did to fix this issue.
I did these steps after adding the node back to the cluster:
1. remove that node from the cluster again.
2. change config file to have --master_addresses empty
3. ran yb-master to start the server (idk if this is the correct way to restart a master server)
4. tried adding the node back to the cluster with yb-admin but got error on connections  and reflected in admin ui
5. change the master.config back and restart the master server with yb-master
6. add it back to the cluster
the node was successfully added back to the cluster but in the admin ui home, there are four servers appeared in the masters section where two of them have the exact same information, even the UUID. The tablet server page is correct. (edited) 

Andrew Liu  2 months ago
And if I try to remove it again, one disappears and one became a non participant. That makes me wonder what is the correct way of restarting a yb-master server, cuz it seems like it started a new yb-master server in the same node and they are sharing some same meta-data files. (edited) 

Bogdan Matican:palm_tree:  2 months ago
@Andrew Liu to follow up on this, I think the issue I linked above is still valid and @Sanketh (YB) is planning on working on a fix for it.
As a higher level question, any particular reason why you are trying to remove and then add back the exact same node? On our end, we primarily use the remove when we decommission nodes, so we don’t generally need to add back the same node…

Andrew Liu  2 months ago
I'm just experimenting with operations on the cluster level, where  there would certainly be cases where we want a certain master to stop taking traffic for a while, do some operations and bring it back up, so I think we still want to be able to add it back.
Also sent to the channel ∙ Starred

Bogdan Matican:palm_tree:  2 months ago
@Andrew Liu Oh I see. Let me drill into that a little bit.
If your going to take a node down temporarily, but intent to bring it back up, you should not need to actually do REMOVE_SERVER:
- If the process is out for a short period of time (used to be 5mins, we’ve increased it to 15m), it will just catch up through RPCs when it comes back up
- If the process is out for longer, then it will go through what we refer to as Remote Bootstrap, where the current leader will forward it all the relevant files to catch up
You likely only really need the REMOVE_SERVER command in case you decide you’re not bringing this node back up at all. Say you took it down for maintenance but realize that the disk is bad, so instead of a temporary stop, you want to decommission and bring in a new node.
That being said, the command is still something we’re planning to fix!

Andrew Liu  2 months ago
Got it! Thank you! Ill look into remote boostrapping!

Bogdan Matican:palm_tree:  2 months ago
That will just happen automatically.
You can just test by stopping the master for a couple of minutes vs for longer and bringing it back, without any yb-admin commands to remove it!
Added to your starred items

Steve Bang  2 months ago
Sounds like good content to add to the 'yb-admin' docs for that

issue.title: [docdb] Master falling behind does not get automatically remote bootstrapped

labels.name: kind/enhancement
labels.description: This is an enhancement of an existing feature

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-1842](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-1842)
Currently, if a master falls behind to the point that the leader no longer has logs, or its follower unavailability window passes (default 15m for both), it would require manual intervention to remove it from the quorum and add it back.

At the raft level, we have this flag to control w/e or nor to evict failed followers: `evict_failed_followers`. This is disabled for masters though, as there is no automated mechanism for them to be added back into the quorum!

Moreover, until #2007 is resolved, the current steps of issuing a remove, followed by an add, require that in between, we actually wipe the master data and start back the master in shell mode (empty `master_addresses` flag).

Ideally, we'd have some mechanic through which we would automatically trigger a remote bootstrap for the master, if it comes back after the default 15m window.

cc @iSignal @hectorgcr

issue.title: [docs] Update descriptions of master_addresses="" for standby mode

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Based on #2007, which mentions setting `--master_addresses` to an empty string (`"") when removing or adding YB-Master servers:

- Add descriptions to relevant configuration flags about using "standby" mode (`--master_addresses=""`) for adding and removing servers:
  - For `yb-master`: [`--master_addresses`](https://docs.yugabyte.com/latest/reference/configuration/yb-master/#master-addresses)
  - For `yb-admin`: [`change_master_config ADD_SERVER | REMOVE_SERVER`](https://docs.yugabyte.com/latest/admin/yb-admin/#change-master-config)
  - Others? When does it make sense to use standby mode?
  - Expected behavior of starting in standby mode? From [@iSignal comment](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/issues/2007#issuecomment-529032099)
    - deletes all directories under `yb-data`, including logs, rocksdb, and instance metadata . Preserves the google logs directory.
    - We need to retain some of the root level dirs so that the server can bootstrap once again and also preserve instance metadata so that the uuid that is used by the server in memory is preserved across restarts.

@iSignal @bmatican Getting answers is somewhat urgent for mentioning standby mode and its behavior in an open PR (#4676) and for doc'ing it in the reference --seems important to add ASAP.
